title: Address billing drift from tokenizer upgrades and cross-model tokenization inconsistencies
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Summary: We've observed intermittent billing discrepancies after a tokenizer patch and during model-fallback scenarios. The root cause appears to be that token counts are computed with differing tokenizer binaries (model-specific encoders or upgraded shared tokenizer) at request time and later during reconciliation, leading to non-deterministic billing for the same user prompt. This ticket scopes analysis and a mitigation plan to make metering deterministic across tokenizer upgrades and cross-model routing/fallbacks.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy two model variants: model-v1 (old tokenizer) and model-v2 (updated tokenizer) behind the same endpoint with smart routing that falls back from v2->v1 under capacity pressure.
2) Send identical batch of 10k prompts that include edge cases (emoji, mixed-language, non-space-separated tokens, long UTF-8 sequences, and rare punctuation) to the endpoint.
3) Force fallback for a subset of requests so they execute on v1 after initial attempt on v2 (simulate capacity/timeout fallback).
4) Compare per-request token_count stored in request logs (what runtime recorded at generation time) vs. billing pipeline token_count used for invoicing/reconciliation.
5) Run a tokenizer upgrade (v2) rollout while keeping historical records; re-run reconciliation for the same 10k prompts and observe differences in billed token counts.

Expected result: Token counts remain stable across fallback and upgrades. Observed result: ~0.6% of requests show >1 token delta (up to 4 tokens) causing customer-visible invoice drift in test dataset.
notes_and_discussion: 02/16 sync: initial triage with serving/runtime teams. We believe mismatch arises from two factors: (A) model-specific tokenizer differences (vocab/merges) and (B) token counts stored as 'runtime_calc' while biller re-tokenizes using current canonical tokenizer.

02/18 design review: PM suggests versioning tokenizer at request capture time and persisting tokenizer_version with raw content; infra concerned about storage & re-tokenization CPU cost for backfills.
02/22 trade-off: Option to bill by UTF-8 bytes proposed; simpler and stable but less representative of tokenized compute cost across models (may under/over-charge relative to model compute).
02/26 legal/finance: Prefer solution that enables deterministic auditability for credits and disputes. Finance requires ability to re-derive counts for at least 90 days for audits.

03/03 note: Edge case with streaming retries — when a stream is retried mid-response the runtime increments token_count in fragments; different tokenizer can change fragment boundary tokenization causing double or missing attribution.
proposed_solution: Primary approach (recommended): Record the tokenizer identifier and model-encoder checksum at request capture time, and persist the raw user input (or a compressed representation) with the usage record. Biller uses the recorded tokenizer binary (from an immutable storage of tokenizer artifacts) to reproduce token_count deterministically during reconciliation.

Fallback approach: If storing raw text is prohibitive, record both the runtime_token_count (what runtime computed) and the canonical UTF-8 byte_length. Use runtime_token_count as primary for billing and byte_length for cross-checks; require CI gating for any tokenizer upgrade that changes runtime_token_count distributions beyond a threshold.

Complementary: Add a gating test in release pipeline that runs a token-delta detector on a representative prompt corpus and blocks tokenizer rollouts that exceed configured thresholds for token-count drift.

Streaming-specific fix: Ensure that streaming retry logic snapshots fragment tokenizer state (or the incremental token_count delta and tokenizer_version) at each resume point so replays use the same tokenizer context during metering attribution.
tradeoffs: Persisting raw input increases storage and needs tighter access controls (PII concerns). Finance wants reproducibility; security wants limited retention. Compromise: compress and encrypt inputs and limit retention to 90 days with audit logging on access.

Keeping runtime_token_count as ground-truth avoids re-tokenization compute cost but makes audits impossible if runtime has bugs. Storing tokenizer artifacts increases ops surface area (artifact registry + retention policy).

UTF-8 byte billing is cheap and stable but will produce charge divergences from actual model tokenized compute — could be seen as unfair by customers with many short tokens that encode to many bytes or vice versa.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a synthetic test corpus of 50k prompts covering multi-language, emojis, and edge punctuation, token-count delta between runtime and billing must be <= 0.05% for >90% of prompts after fix rollout.
2) All new tokenizer/model deployments must include a 'token-delta' CI check. CI must fail if median token delta vs. current canonical tokenizer is > 0.25% on the representative corpus.

3) Update metering records to include tokenizer_version for all new requests within 2 weeks of rollout start. Historical data must be backfilled for last 90 days where feasible and flagged in billing reconciliations.
4) Streaming retries must carry fragment-level token deltas and tokenizer_version so that billing can deterministically attribute incremental tokens without duplication.
5) Documentation and runbook for finance and support on how to repro and resolve billing disputes is published (Confluence link in ticket).
testing_plan: Unit tests for tokenizer-versioned billing code that simulate 10k prompts across 3 tokenizer versions and assert stable billing counts.
Integration test: deploy a shadow billing job that re-tokenizes using stored tokenizer artifact and compares to runtime_token_count; produce daily drift reports to SLO 'metering-drift'.
Chaos test: Simulate streaming retries and model fallbacks; ensure no double-charges and per-request billed token_count equals runtime token_count recorded at generation time.
Performance impact: measure additional CPU for backfill re-tokenization (estimate 200k re-tokenizations/hour per 8 vCPU worker) and plan capacity.
rollout_plan: 1) Short-term (hotfix): Stop re-tokenizing at biller time for new events — prefer using runtime_token_count as authoritative while we implement artifacts registry. This reduces immediate variance.

2) Mid-term (release): Implement tokenizer artifact registry (immutable, versioned), persist tokenizer_version in usage records, and update billing pipeline to re-tokenize only when tokenizer_version present or to use stored runtime_token_count as canonical.
3) Backfill: Run a prioritized backfill for the last 90 days for high-value customers and any flagged invoices where drift > threshold; compute credits if necessary.
4) Policy: Add release gating and a token-delta CI check for tokenizer/model deploys. Communicate policy to model onboarding docs.
5) Post-rollout: Monitor 'metering-drift' dashboard for 30 days; if any customer-impacting regressions appear issue immediate credits and post-mortem.
